risk_if_not_implemented: Without Risk Response, risks may remain unidentified, unowned or unmanaged, leaving decision-makers without a defensible basis for prioritization and treatment. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Incident Persistence / Recurrence (R-IR-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Change Management Program
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of a change management program.
compensating_control_1.justification: Change Management Program (CHG-02) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Risk Response (RSK-16) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Vulnerability Remediation Process
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that vulnerabilities are properly identified, tracked and remediated.
compensating_control_2.justification: Vulnerability Remediation Process (VPM-06) provides vulnerability management that compensates for the absence of Risk Response (RSK-16) by reducing the exploitable attack surface by addressing known weaknesses before they are leveraged. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
